html:
An uprising in Taiwan in 1947 against the Nationalist government of the Republic of China, put down with mass killings. It is named after the date it began.

Japan had ruled Taiwan from 1895 to 1945. When Japan lost the war, the island was handed to Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists, the Kuomintang. The governor Chen Yi and officials from the mainland treated the Taiwanese as suspect, took the best posts and property, and ran the economy into inflation and shortages.

On 27 February 1947, agents of the tobacco monopoly in Taipei beat a woman selling untaxed cigarettes, and a bystander was shot dead. The next day protests spread across the island, and local committees took control of many towns and demanded reform. Chen Yi pretended to negotiate while troops came from the mainland. From early March soldiers killed thousands, perhaps 18,000 to 28,000, many of them lawyers, teachers and other leading Taiwanese.

The event began decades of martial law, during which it could not be discussed. In 1995 the president apologised, and 28 February is now a memorial day.
sum: An uprising in Taiwan in 1947 against the Nationalist government of the Republic of China, put down with mass killings. It is named after the date it began.
